_notes_added_2026-10-23: Independent verification found the day-fixed-effects regression's reported standard error used residual degrees of freedom = n-2 (418) rather than n minus the 128 day-dummy parameters (approx. 291). Recomputing with the correct df widens the SE slightly but does not change the conclusion: the coefficient (-0.122, originally reported SE 0.360) is nowhere close to significant either way (p=0.73 at df=418; still far from significant at the smaller correct df). No headline number or conclusion changes.

check_1_does_magnitude_predict_position.description: Is ann_vol_20d_pct itself more extreme when the tool happens to be called last? (full unmatched pool, n=754)
check_1_does_magnitude_predict_position.verdict: No (p=0.28) -- the magnitude of the number does not predict whether it gets called last.

check_2_does_reliance_ratio_differ.description: If the agent calls it last "because it intends to rely on it most," the ratio expected_vol_pct/ann_vol_20d_pct should be HIGHER when is_last=True. It is not: 0.223 (is_last=True) vs 0.223 (is_last=False), see step2_results.
check_2_does_reliance_ratio_differ.verdict: No detectable difference -- this specific version of the confound story is not supported by the data.

check_3_session_length_confound.description: Total tool calls per session (excluding submit_decision) differs sharply by is_last group: sessions where get_volatility_stats is called last are systematically SHORTER sessions.
check_3_session_length_confound.verdict: YES, real and large (p<1e-15) -- mechanically true in part because "called last" caps how many more calls can follow, but it also means is_last is confounded with "this was a shorter, more decisive session" in general, not purely with calling-position. We could not rule this out as an independent channel. It does not change the headline here (the effect we looked for was null anyway), but it means a different, positive-finding dataset using the same is_last design would still need to separately control for session length before attributing an effect to position per se.

confound_discussion.overall_assessment: The confound that the task flagged (intent-driven calling order) is not supported by the two direct checks we could run (magnitude does not predict position; reliance ratio does not differ by position). A second, different confound (session length/thoroughness) is real and sizeable, but is moot for THIS result because the position effect itself was null on every cut. We flag it because a future test with a positive finding on this corpus would need to address it.
confound_discussion.threat: Does the agent call get_volatility_stats LAST specifically WHEN it intends to rely on it most (a different causal story than "position itself causes weight")?

corpus: data/mechanisms/sessions/newsagent, FULL arm, temperature=1.0 runs only (file pattern FULL_{0,1,2,3}.json.gz; the FULL_T06_* temperature-0.6 files were excluded per the task spec), 250 ticker-days x up to 4 k-runs = 1000 session files attempted.

extraction_rules.is_last_definition: Among trace entries that are literal tool-call records (have a "tool" key -- this excludes the separate "turn" entries that just list which tools the model decided to call), get_volatility_stats is is_last=True iff it is the entry immediately preceding the submit_decision tool-call entry, i.e. zero other tool-call entries sit between them.
extraction_rules.tool_result_parsing: Tool "result" fields are JSON-encoded strings; parsed with json.loads before reading fields.
extraction_rules.usable_session_filter: d["valid"] is True; trace parses; exactly one get_volatility_stats call; exactly one submit_decision call and it is the final tool-call entry; submit_decision.args has a numeric expected_vol_pct; get_volatility_stats's result JSON has ann_vol_20d_pct.

sample_accounting.key_structural_fact: ann_vol_20d_pct is IDENTICAL across every k-run of the same day_id (checked all 250 days with >=1 usable session: 0 days show any variation). This is expected -- the tool is a deterministic function of the as_of price history, which is the same for every k-run of a given ticker-day -- and it is what makes the matched-day design a clean natural experiment: within a matched day, MAGNITUDE is held exactly fixed and only calling POSITION (and the free-running generation) differs across k-runs.

stats_methods.binomial_test: Exact two-sided binomial test via math.comb (same definition as scipy.stats.binomtest / R binom.test), validated against a known value (k=15,n=20,p=.5 -> p=0.04139).
stats_methods.diff_of_slopes: Welch-style z-test on the difference of two independent slope estimates, SE_diff=sqrt(se1^2+se2^2).
stats_methods.fisher_z: Pearson r 95% CI via Fisher z-transform, SE=1/sqrt(n-3).
stats_methods.note: scipy and statsmodels are not installed in the project .venv; all statistics below are closed-form / numpy, implemented in src/finagent/mechanisms/proximity_stats.py.
stats_methods.ols: Simple OLS slope/intercept/SE from residual variance (textbook formulas), validated by the identity t_slope == t_r.
stats_methods.student_t_cdf: Regularized incomplete beta function via Lentz continued fraction (the classical Numerical-Recipes algorithm scipy itself is built on); validated against known critical values (t=2.228,df=10 -> p=0.0500; t=1.96,df=1000 -> p=0.0503).
stats_methods.wilson_ci: Wilson score interval for a binomial proportion.

step2_results.headline: NO detectable position effect on reliance, by every cut tried: slope difference p=0.59 (matched days) / p=0.67 (full unmatched pool); day-fixed-effects level test p=0.73; paired per-day t-test p=0.55; the mean expected_vol_pct / ann_vol_20d_pct ratio is 0.223 (SE 0.014, n=162) when last vs 0.223 (SE 0.009, n=258) when not last -- indistinguishable. This is a genuine, reasonably powered null (n=420 across 128 independently-matched days), not an absence of testing.
step2_results.method: Within the 128 matched days (420 sessions), regress expected_vol_pct on ann_vol_20d_pct separately in the is_last=True and is_last=False subsamples (simple OLS, closed-form, SE from residual variance). Also run a day-fixed-effects regression (day-demean both variables then regress) and a plain paired per-day mean-difference t-test, both of which exploit the fact that ann_vol_20d_pct is day-constant to isolate the pure LEVEL effect of position, holding magnitude exactly fixed. Difference of the two slopes tested with a Welch-style z-test (SE_diff = sqrt(se1^2+se2^2); scipy/statsmodels are not installed in this venv, so p-values use a from-scratch Student-t CDF built on the regularized incomplete-beta continued-fraction algorithm, validated against known reference values -- see stats_methods below).

step3_results.planned_test: Compare, in log space, whether submitted expected_vol_pct sits closer to a LATER-called tool's volatility number than an EARLIER-called one, using get_volatility_stats.ann_vol_20d_pct vs get_risk_budget.trailing_vol_20d_pct as the task's suggested pair.
step3_results.reason: get_risk_budget.trailing_vol_20d_pct is computed by the identical formula as get_volatility_stats.ann_vol_20d_pct (_sd(returns[-20:]) * sqrt(252), see src/finagent/harness/toolbox.py) on the same as_of price history. In all n=32 sessions where both tools were each called exactly once, the two reported numbers were EXACTLY equal (to the 1-decimal rounding both tools use). There is therefore no pair of genuinely different numbers for the agent's answer to be "closer to one than the other" -- the test is vacuous by construction, not underpowered. We checked the rest of the registered toolset (src/finagent/harness/toolbox.py, 31 tools) for any other pair of distinct, comparable-scale volatility-relevant outputs from two different tools: the only other candidate, get_event_risk.avg_abs_daily_move_pct, co-occurs with get_volatility_stats in only 11/1000 sessions (too few) and is on a different scale/definition (mean absolute daily return over the full history vs. a 20-day realized stdev), which would introduce exactly the kind of forced, misleading comparison the task asked us to avoid. We report the tie finding itself (n=32, 32/32 identical) rather than substitute a confounded pair.

task: Proximity/recency: does a number's position in the tool-call sequence (distance from submit_decision) predict how much weight the agent gives it, independent of the number's magnitude?
